items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: Loch Lomond is a song title mentioned in the context of the interviewee's repertoire and recording history, not a person.

ctx.x:
No. My big song in Pittsburgh -- that is, getting into the swing and the classy bit was "Trees". But we never recorded that.

You see, when I came to New York -- let's face it, you had a whole lot of singers here already. I think Claude was sort of wise to select these things like "Loch Lomond" and "Annie Laurie" -- was that at least make it a little different from just an average vocalist (singing) in front of the band.

And it isn't a novelty. Claude may have known what he was doing, because I knew from nothing…
So he really was responsible for decisions to use that material?
